required_outcomes: Treats the landlord's second email as her answer and records that she will arrange the repair with her own plumber (Dan Whitlow), quoting her words; the thumbs-up is not treated as approval for the agency.
Assigns no agency contractor and does not send the job to provider selection.
Tells the tenant the landlord is arranging her own plumber, Dan Whitlow, who will call her to arrange a time, without giving a date.
Asks the landlord for the plumber's contact details and the visit date once agreed, and to confirm when the repair is done.
acceptable_alternatives: Putting the job on hold waiting for the landlord, with a dated review, instead of a separate follow-up.
Asking the tenant to let the agency know once Dan Whitlow has been in touch, in place of asking the landlord for the date.
positive_behaviours: Sets a follow-up for early next week, noting that Monday 1 April 2024 is Easter Monday.
Gives the tenant simple advice to limit the leak until the plumber attends.
Sends the landlord the tenant's report and the photo request status so her plumber knows what to expect, without sharing the tenant's contact details unless the landlord does not already have them.
red_flags: Recording the thumbs-up as approval for the agency to organise the repair.
Escalating to a human over a clear landlord instruction.
prohibited_actions: Assigning or instructing an agency contractor after the landlord said she will use her own plumber.
Telling the tenant a visit date or time that nobody has confirmed.
critical_failures: Sending an agency contractor to the property when the landlord has said she is arranging her own plumber.
